items.bodyExcerpt:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8091. With untied embeddings, FSDP2 shards `lm_head` independently, but fused forwards read its weight from the parent. This bypasses the head's unsharding, mixed precision, CPU offload and backward hooks. A two-GPU Qwen3 reproducer fails with mixed Tensor/DTensor operands (Torch), BF16/FP32 operands (Triton), or CPU weights under offload.

Run the fused projection through an FSDP-registered forward method on the existing head. The head keeps its own sharding group and ordinary logits `forward`; backend selection and label preparation remain unchanged. The dense, Qwen2-VL, Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.5 and GLM4V adapters share this entry point.

Related work: closed #7427 instead keeps the fused head in the root FSDP unit. Open #8004 adds an opt-in FP32 head and routes that branch through its head forward, while the default fused path still reads the weight directly. Open #5948 falls back to materialized logits for a sharded Qwen3-VL Torch head; this change retains fused computation and also fixes the default dense and other adapter paths. items.title: [RFC]: Support ViT Full CUDA Graph (Tracker)
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Motivation.

Multimodal large language models (e.g., Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.5, GLM-V, Kimi K2.5) rely on a Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder to process visual inputs before feeding them into the language model backbone. In production serving scenarios, the ViT forward pass involves launching a large number of small CUDA kernels — including patch embedding, layer normalization, multi-head self-attention, and MLP projections — each of which incurs non-trivial kernel launch overhead on the host side.

Currently, vLLM supports CUDA graph capture for the decoder (LLM) portion of the model, which has proven effective at reducing kernel launch costs and improving throughput. However, the ViT encoder is still executed eagerly, meaning every forward pass re-launches all kernels from scratch. Extending full CUDA graph support to the ViT encoder would allow the entire encoder forward pass to be captured and replayed as a single graph, eliminating per-kernel launch overhead and enabling more consistent, low-latency inference for multimodal models.

items.title: [Bug] `ep_gather` output store overflows int32 with DeepEP v2 expanded layout (IMA in `_fwd_kernel_ep_gather`)
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Summary

`_fwd_kernel_ep_gather` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/deep_gemm_utils.py` computes the output row offset as `cur_token * output_tensor_stride0` in int32. With hidden size K = 6144, this wraps once the output has more than 2^31 / 6144 = 349,525 rows. The store then lands out of bounds and faults with `cudaErrorIllegalAddress`.

#53914 (fe284ea17d) fixed the matching **input** read (`source_token_index_i64 * input_tensor_stride0`). The **output** store is still int32 on main (9ed81581, line 410):

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/9ed81581a896a5bf0448b26d43f52486a435f799/vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/deep_gemm_utils.py#L405-L413

```python
        tl.store(
            output_tensor
            + cur_token * output_tensor_stride0   # int32 * int32
            + cur_block * BLOCK_D
            + off_d,
            ...
```

With the DeepEP v2 all2all backend, the gather receives an **expanded** layout: `recv_topk_ids` is `(rows, 1)`, with one row per (token, local expert) pair. So the output has as many rows as the permuted input, and both offsets hit the same limit. When `topk_ids` is `(tokens, topk)`, the output has one row per received token and normally stays far below the limit, which is presumably why this hasn't shown up before.

## Setup

- GLM-5.2-FP8 (K = 6144, 256 experts, top-8), `--moe-backend deep_gemm`, `--all2all-backend deepep_v2` (hybrid mode)
- 4 nodes × 8 × H100, DP4 × PCP8 (DCP8), TP1, EP32, eager
- vLLM from #57075 at bf0dca88, with the #53914 `ep_gather` input fix applied on top
- `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096` (8192 fails the same way, sooner)

With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, the first memory-profiling forward (`determine_available_memory` → `profile_run`) faults in the gather on the busiest EP rank:

items.title: [Bug][KV Connector] MultiConnector on prefill silently disables the hybrid KV cache manager, so a NixlConnector decode rejects every transfer with an opaque "NIXL compatibility hash mismatch"
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment
vLLM v0.31.0 (CUDA 13.0 image), nixl 1.4.1 (LIBFABRIC backend over EFA), 2 nodes, TP8 per node, B300. Model zai-org/GLM-5.3 (DeepSeek-V3.2-style: MLA + DSA indexer cache), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, MTP 1, `--block-size 64`.

### Describe the bug
Prefill/decode disaggregation works with `NixlConnector` on both sides. To keep CPU KV offload on the prefill node, we switched only the prefill instance to a `MultiConnector`:

```json
{"kv_connector": "MultiConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both",
 "kv_connector_extra_config": {"connectors": [
   {"kv_connector": "NixlConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_connector_extra_config": {"backends": ["LIBFABRIC"]}},
   {"kv_connector": "LMCacheConnectorV1", "kv_role": "kv_both"}]}}
```

The decode instance kept plain `NixlConnector`. On startup the prefill logs:

```
WARNING [vllm.py] Turning off hybrid kv cache manager because `--kv-transfer-config` selects a KV connector that does not support it.
```

The decode instance keeps the hybrid KV cache manager on (NixlConnector supports it). From then on every request fails on decode at the handshake:

```
File ".../kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py", line 1101, in _nixl_handshake
    raise RuntimeError(
RuntimeError: NIXL compatibility hash mismatch. Local: ac9aa5b3…, Remote: d6e05114…
```

## Summary

With cross-layer index sharing, only some attention layers update the shared top-k buffer.
The old path still remapped that buffer on every layer.

This PR runs the remap only when the layer owns an indexer. For GLM-5.2 with
`index_topk_freq = 4`, this reduces remaps from 78 to 21 per forward pass.

- Layer 0 always owns an indexer, so the shared output is initialized before reuse.

## Purpose

Adds an AITER-backed fusion path for the ROCm `deepseek_v32` (DeepSeek Sparse
Attention) forward, used by both DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.2. The existing
shared-Triton fusion path is untouched and remains the default; the AITER path
is selected at runtime per fusion via opt-in env flags, so behaviour on ROCm is
unchanged unless a flag is set.

This PR is stacked on top of: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51915, so needs enablement to land first before this fusion add-on.

**1. MLA dual RMSNorm** 
Fuses the q and kv-a RMSNorms into one AITER call
(`fused_mla_dual_rms_norm_out`). An out-variant was added so the norms write
model-owned buffers rather than allocating per layer, which lets the call be
hoisted out of the eager region and captured by cudagraph. Also wires the
per-token-quant variant for the quantized case.

**2. Fused QK RoPE + concat + MLA cache write**

concat and KV-cache-write steps on the MLA path. The uint8 KV cache allocated by

AITER op rejects the raw uint8 buffer.

indexer layers.

itself.

independently of the fused variant.

## Summary

- route rope-free sparse MLA to the ROCm Triton implementation for every KV-cache dtype
- dequantize FP8 KV rows in the Triton ragged-prefill kernel using the layer KV scale while keeping Q in model dtype
- use 64-bit query-row offsets so wide, long-context prefills cannot overflow 32-bit pointer arithmetic

## Problem

AITER precompiled sparse MLA kernels assume the DeepSeek cache-row geometry: 512 latent elements plus 64 RoPE elements. GLM-5.3-Flash is rope-free and stores a 512-element row. ## Purpose

`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` is silently ignored for GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`): `Glm5NextMoE` builds `FusedMoE` with `n_shared_experts=None`, so each of the 42 MoE layers still runs the shared expert as a separate MLP (two FP8 block-scale GEMMs, a clamped SiLU and a quant) and adds it to the routed output.

items.title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Pass per-sequence context lengths to the AITER paged MQA-logits kernels
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Error

MTP with native DSA-indexer decode above `next_n=2` crashes during warm-up on MI355X (seen at `next_n=3` and `next_n=6`). GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4, `num_speculative_tokens=5` (`next_n=6`), Gluon paged MQA logits:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-4 (Agent handle: 0x20465ea0) on address 0x792dc0bf1000. Reason: Unknown.
```

Where it does not crash, the indexer silently uses wrong causal bounds: in a direct call at `next_n=3`, the 8192-token sequence loses its last 2 valid positions in every row (9/12 rows correct).

## Cause

With native decode (`next_n > 1`), `rocm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` receives a `(B, next_n)` table of per-row context lengths, `[b, j] = L_b - next_n + j + 1`, built in [`indexer.py#L1136-L1152`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/2df122e65e87dc12870ce5f0180b49f012e7a53b/vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py#L1136-L1152). The AITER Gluon `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits` and `deepgemm_fp8_paged_mqa_logits_stage1` kernels read the table as a flat `[B]` array and some sequences get another row's length.

Example: 4 requests, `next_n=3`, context lengths 8192 / 1500 / 3000 / 700:

| `b` | `j=0` | `j=1` | `j=2` | `L_b` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 8190 | 8191 | **8192** | 8192 |
| 1 | 1498 | 1499 | **1500** | 1500 |
| 2 | 2998 | 2999 | **3000** | 3000 |
| 3 | 698 | 699 | **700** | 700 |

The kernel expects `[8192, 1500, 3000, 700]` and computes each row's bound itself. Reading the `(4, 3)` table as `[4]`, it gets the first four values in memory, `[8190, 8191, 8192, 1498]`: request 0 loses its last 2 positions in every row, and requests 1 to 3 get lengths past their own KV pages, the likely source of the fault. Column `j = next_n - 1` equals `L_b`, which is what the kernel needs.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

With MTP and prefix caching on, hybrid models such as GLM-5.3-Flash can return garbage when a request reuses a cached prompt prefix. Some prefill steps save a checkpoint of the linear-attention state in the middle of a chunk. In those steps the scheduler leaves an unused MTP scratch block in the slot that belongs to the checkpoint. That block is never written, yet it is registered in the prefix cache ahead of the real checkpoint, so later requests resume from it. This change moves the scratch block out of the way in those steps too, as already happens in every other step.

The skip was added together with internal checkpoints in #53614. GLM-5.3-Flash reaches this path since #56960. The branch is based on current main (58b3298457). No open PR changes speculative-block relocation; #57128 changes the Mamba lookup and does not touch this path.

- Fixes persistent garbage output after prefix-cache hits for hybrid models with internal prefill checkpoints and MTP, for example GLM-5.3-Flash with `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'`.
- No behavior change without speculative decoding, for `mamba_cache_mode` other than `align`, or for steps without an internal checkpoint.

## Overview

`--dcp-gather` runs decode context parallelism (DCP) for MLA models whose attention backends can't run DCP natively.

- Before each layer's attention, every rank pulls the batch's pages from the other ranks into a scratch cache, and attention runs as if DCP were off. Attention backends are unmodified.
- The pull runs on a side stream through symmetric memory, overlapped with the previous layer's output projection and MoE.
- DeepSeek-V4, which has no native DCP, always uses it.

## Overview

Fix garbage output when a DCP group spans TP × PCP (e.g. TP2 × PCP2 × DCP4): sort each DCP group's ranks so `rank_in_group` agrees with the order collectives return shards in.

## Claims

- TP2 × PCP2 × DCP4 on GLM-5.3-NVFP4 goes from GSM8K 0.000 to 0.905.
- No change for DCP groups that were already ascending (DCP within TP, or DCP == PCP), which covers every previously validated configuration.

## Validation

GSM8K (5-shot) on 4x B300, MRV2, GLM-5.3-NVFP4, `-tp 2 -pcp 2 -dcp 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla -cc.cudagraph_mode=NONE`:

| this PR | 0.905 |

```bash
pytest tests/distributed/test_dcp_a2a.py -k test_dcp_group_ranks_match_collective_order  # 5 passed
```

## Details

**Root cause.** With PCP, `initialize_model_parallel` builds a DCP group that spans TP × PCP PCP-first (`all_ranks.transpose(-1, -2)`), giving member lists like `[0, 2, 1, 3]`.
- `torch.distributed.new_group` sorts its ranks, so all-gathers return shards in global-rank order.
- `GroupCoordinator.rank_in_group` is `ranks.index(rank)` on the unsorted list.
- The DCP LSE merge (`correct_attn_out`) uses `rank_in_group` to pick this rank's LSE from the gathered LSEs. So DCP ranks 1 and 2 rescaled their partial outputs with each other's LSE.

The new unit test checks that DCP groups are ascending for TP-only, PCP-only and TP × PCP layouts.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

HiSparse decode is CPU-bound on main because of one scheduler-side scan. Every step, `HiSparseCoordinator.all_context_pages_resident` walks every page of every scheduled request in every resident group (one group per layer), only to decide whether prefill can skip host staging. That is O(requests × context pages × layers) Python per step, even for pure-decode batches.

The scan arrived in c4b9b7deac ("bypass host resolution for resident decode"), after the GLM-5.3 results in #53781 were measured, and shipped with 3/N. This PR caches the requests whose resident pages are all non-null. A request is scanned once. Pages become null only at admission or host import, before the first scan, or when the pool reuses an unpinned page (`_lose_page`), so those paths plus `free` drop the cache entry. The per-step check is O(requests).

items.title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Carry adopted prefix pages in the new request's row
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #60109: HiSparse servers crash with an illegal memory access when a new request hits a prefix whose published host pages still have GPU copies.

The coordinator adopts those copies after the scheduler has already built the request's `NewRequestData`, so the adopted row went out as a `block_table_updates` entry. For a new request, model runner V2 then stages two full-row writes for the same row in one step (`add_requests`, then `update_requests`), and the staged-write kernel applies them in parallel with no ordering. A rank that kept the pre-adoption row saw null resident pages, while the scheduler reported every context page resident. The resident-prefill shortcut then sent the prefill rows through the decode residency resolver, whose host union overflowed `max_union_rows` and faulted.

The fix puts the adopted row in the new request's `block_ids`; `block_table_updates` stays for running requests. HiSparse-only (`hisparse/connector.py`).

Note: MRv2's staged block-table writer doesn't order overlapping writes to the same row. This PR stops HiSparse from producing them; changing that in core is a separate discussion.

## Reproduction on main

GLM-5.3-NVFP4 on B200, either TP8 or TP4 (`host_pool_gib` 128 or 64):

items.title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Write a new request's block-table update once
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Fixes #60109 (HiSparse servers crash with an illegal memory access on prefix hits).

A `block_table_updates` row supersedes a request's normal block-table write, and `update_requests` already skips `new_block_ids` for running requests that have one. New requests lacked that guard. `add_requests` staged the `NewRequestData` row, `update_requests` staged the update, both for the same row in the same step, and `_apply_write_kernel` applies staged writes as unordered programs. Ranks could keep either row. With HiSparse prefix-copy adoption, ranks that kept the stale row read null resident pages, and the decode residency resolver overflowed.

Fix: `add_requests` skips the `NewRequestData` row when a table update exists, and `update_requests` writes the update as before.

## Why this instead of #60117

- **It fixes the race where it happens.** MRv2 accepts two unordered writes to one row; #60117 only stops today's single producer (HiSparse) from sending them.
- **It's smaller and symmetric.** Five lines extend the guard `update_requests` already has. #60117 instead has the HiSparse connector rewrite an already-built `NewRequestData`, which also changes what every other reader of that field sees.
- **It costs nothing for other users.** A dict lookup per new request, and one fewer GPU row write when an update exists.

Tradeoff: this touches `gpu/model_runner.py`, while #60117 is HiSparse-only.

items.title: [Spec Decode][GLM-5.3-Flash] Support adaptive verification
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Motivation

Adaptive verification chooses on the GPU how many draft tokens to verify for each request. During full CUDA graph replay, the physical token buffer and captured control flow remain fixed, while the live request boundaries can change. GLM-5.3-Flash previously made two assumptions that were incompatible with this behavior:

- GDN captured the ordinary one-token decode path, even though replay could group those token rows into fewer requests with multiple verification tokens.
- The k-pool scatter path assumed every physical token row belonged to a live request, but a replayed graph can contain additional padding rows.

This PR updates both paths to handle GPU-selected request lengths and graph padding.

## Changes

- Allow the GDN backend to replay CUDA graphs whose per-request query lengths are chosen on the GPU.
- Capture GDN’s speculative path and the k-pool indexer at the maximum configured verification width.
- Update the k-pool scatter path to safely discard CUDA graph padding without synchronizing lengths back to the CPU.
- Add tests for variable verification lengths, graph padding, and sparse-indexer alignment.

## Testing

Added and ran focused tests covering:

- Mixed per-request GDN verification lengths
- CUDA graph padding in the k-pool scatter path
- Sparse-indexer sequence-length alignment
- Capture-time and replay-time request partition differences

## Throughput results

I benchmarked GLM-5.3-Flash with MTP on four B300 GPUs (TEP4). The sweep covered:

- Speculative depths `kmax = 1...5`

`VllmConfig` ends post-init by logging `Enabled custom fusions: ...`, but the passes only run under `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE`. - No `Enabled custom fusions` log when compilation is off (for example DeepSeek V3.2/V4, GLM-5, Kimi K3, MiniMax M3 and Qwen4Exp with their default breakable CUDA graphs).
